I’ve always liked the idea of crypto helping fund energy, housing, and other real-world infrastructure.

At the very least, it's a much better use of crypto than memecoins.

@loafmarkets is taking that idea pretty far with Project Amber.

Think of it as turning a private solar project into an onchain market, giving investors exposure to its value and yield without owning the asset itself.

That could change who gets access to these investments, since projects like this usually:

→ Sit in private markets
→ Come with high barriers to entry
→ Offer limited liquidity

Loaf’s idea is to make that exposure easier to access and much easier to trade.

But the upside goes beyond the investor. The money is ultimately tied to infrastructure that produces electricity for homes and businesses.

This is the side of RWAs I’d love to see grow. ٩(◕‿◕)۶

The most common pushback I hear on @Collector_Crypt is that it's "jUsT a gAmBLiNg pLaTfOrm" and "gaChA iSnT suStAinAbLe"

It's simply just wrong, and the @Blockworks data proves it:

Start with the chart most people skip. Wallets holding at least one tokenized collectible, and this is with Gachapon wallets excluded. We are at 18,000+ wallets already, and the curve is steepening into October. 

Those wallets hold $28.9M of insured collectibles across 98,235 cards sitting in the vault right now.

More telling: wallets holding more than one card went from 3k to 8k this year. People aren't trying it once and leaving. They're accumulating.

But the strongest signal is redemptions.

Redeeming means burning the NFT and having the physical card shipped to your door. It's the most expensive, least liquid, most committed action available on the platform. A gambler never does this. A gambler flips and moves on.

Redemptions just hit an all-time high of $1.7M in a single week, at roughly $8k average per wallet.

People are taking real cards home, actual collectors do collect.

Then look at what they actually hold. Across 18,202 wallets and 98,235 cards, average card value scales from $52 in the smallest portfolios to $3,451 in the largest. A 66x step-up. Collectors moving up tiers aren't buying more volume, but they're buying better cards. That's exactly what a real collector does.

633 wallets hold a card worth over $1,000. Two hold cards worth $1M. Shout out to @charred_io here.

To sum it up: the gacha has just been the Trojan horse to get enough supply onchain to attract the right collectors. 

What's actually happening though is what's always been the bullcase from day 1: Collector slowly but surely becoming the superior marketplace that collectors trust and collect on.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 6 OCTOBER 2026

Higher yields are testing metals. Competition for secure supply keeps building.

🌍 MACRO
US services growth slowed in September, while input-price pressures reached their highest since July 2022. That complicates the Fed outlook: softer activity offers relief, but persistent inflation keeps monetary pressure alive.

☢️ URANIUM
Fuel security is attracting concrete financial commitments. September’s Centrus–Radiant agreement includes customer prepayments to support US enrichment expansion, with HALEU deliveries planned before decade-end.

My read: securing fuel early is becoming part of financing the nuclear buildout. Execution and delivery timelines remain critical.

🥈 SILVER
The firmer dollar and higher yields are near-term headwinds. The Silver Institute still forecasts another supply deficit in 2026, even with weaker industrial demand.

That distinction matters: a deficit can support the longer-term case while macro pressure drives volatility today.

🔌 COPPER
Reuters reports China wants copper concentrate supply assurances before approving the Anglo–Teck merger.

Supply security is entering merger negotiations. Access to feedstock is becoming a strategic priority as smelters compete for material.

🥇 GOLD
Central bankers speaking yesterday reaffirmed gold’s reserve role amid debt concerns and geopolitical instability.

Rising yields increase the cost of holding gold, while diversification demand continues to support its strategic appeal.

💭 MY TAKE
I’m watching the dollar and bond yields for near-term direction, alongside fuel contracts, concentrate availability and project delivery for the longer-term picture.

The strongest conviction comes from following both.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium
